evidence: instruction.md reads as a recruiting lead talking, with first-person plural and singular throughout and no spec-sheet cadence. Line 1: 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day? Two things happen in it.' (short terse sentence after a question). Line 1: 'Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts.' Line 3 mixes clause lengths and semicolons: 'dragging is welcome but optional', 'The order of cards inside a stage is ours to arrange', 'tell me who'. Line 11: 'layout and names are yours. A clear desktop workspace is what matters. We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout.' Line 13: 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call.' Contractions are present (nobody's, people's, don't, it's, mustn't). A grep for marketing/LLM gloss (seamless, robust, delve, leverage, intuitive, elevate, ensure, comprehensive, streamline, empower, em/en dashes) across instruction.md and both notes found zero hits. Paragraph lengths vary (paragraph 5 is one sentence, paragraph 3 is six). The notes keep the same team voice rather than switching to a neutral spec register: hireops_rules.md:3-5 'These are the working rules for HireOps, our recruiting workspace. Follow them exactly. Routes, field names, element ids, button labels and the shape of the pages are yours; what we care about is...'; :43 'and Rejected off to the side'; :127 'between our side and the candidate'; :175 'Where drafts are kept is yours.' Bullets are not mechanically parallel (e.g. :69-73 differ in length and structure; :131-134 are parallel by nature of a permission list, but that is normal for a rules note). The rules note is necessarily denser and structured (headings, tables), which suits a rules document; whether the brief is a spec rather than a request belongs to row 1, not this row. Minor observations that do not rise to a defect: (a) some uncontracted first-person phrasing ('I am typing', 'I am reading', 'I have not sent', instruction.md:5,7) is slightly formal but sits next to contractions in the same file; (b) hireops_rules.md section 8 (:198-202, 'The runtime may launch Node from a working directory other than the application directory... do not rely on inherited shell variables') is in a flatter technical register than the rest of the note, and it is the one place the voice reads like runtime boilerplate; (c) spelling register drifts: instruction.md:13 'honour PORT' vs hireops_rules.md:201 'Honor' and integration.md:7 'honoring' (integration.md is template-controlled and byte-matches the template plus a task-added third paragraph). None of these is robotic, over-polished or marketing prose. Adversarial check: a reader could not tell the brief came from a template generator. The only template-written text is integration.md, which is already terse and plain. No conforming-alternative or broken-app path applies, because this row grades prose, not app behaviour. It needs no runtime evidence, so nothing is missing.
notes: Optional polish, not required: use one spelling, either 'honor' or 'honour'. Integration.md is template-controlled, so the task-owned instruction.md:13 is the line to change. The section 8 runtime paragraph of hireops_rules.md could also be rewritten into the house voice. Neither is a blocker for row 2.
